parts.label: (a)
hints: Hint 1: Start by thinking what decides the sign of $V_{OUT}$ for a comparator. How must $V_{+}$ compare with $V_{-}$ to give -5.0 V at low temperature and +5.0 V at high temperature?

Hint 2: Recall how an NTC thermistor changes. Is its resistance large or small at low temperature, and how would that affect the voltage at the tap of a divider made from the thermistor and a $1000 \, \Omega$ resistor?
Hint 3: Think about using the battery and earth lines to make two dividers. What fixed voltage would two $1000 \, \Omega$ resistors in series give you for a reference?
Hint 4: Decide which divider must go to which input. Which input needs the voltage that rises with temperature so the output switches from negative to positive on warming?
parts.proper_answer: Two potential dividers connected between the top battery lead and the earthed bottom lead. One divider: two $1000 \, \Omega$ resistors in series, tap to $V_{-}$. Other divider: NTC thermistor on top to battery lead and $1000 \, \Omega$ resistor below to earth, tap to $V_{+}$. At low T, $V_{+} < V_{-}$ so $V_{OUT} = -5.0 \text{ V}$; at high T, $V_{+} > V_{-}$ so $V_{OUT} = +5.0 \text{ V}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Recall how a comparator decides**
Think of the op-amp here as just comparing its two inputs. My rule I always use is: $$V_{OUT} = +5.0 \text{ V if } V_{+} > V_{-}$$ $$V_{OUT} = -5.0 \text{ V if } V_{+} < V_{-}$$ You need $V_{OUT} = -5.0 \text{ V}$ when cold and $+5.0 \text{ V}$ when hot. So you need $V_{+} < V_{-}$ when cold and $V_{+} > V_{-}$ when hot. That means $V_{+}$ must rise with temperature while $V_{-}$ stays fixed.

Step 2: **Use the NTC behaviour to make a rising voltage**
An NTC thermistor has high resistance when cold and low resistance when hot. Put it in a divider with a fixed resistor. If the thermistor is at the top (to the positive battery lead) and a $1000 \, \Omega$ resistor is at the bottom (to earth), the tap voltage is: $$V_{+} = V_{batt} \times \frac{1000}{R_{th} + 1000}$$ When $R_{th}$ is large (cold), the fraction is small so $V_{+}$ is small. When $R_{th}$ falls (hot), the fraction grows so $V_{+}$ rises. That is exactly what you need.

Step 3: **Make a fixed reference for the other input**
With the three $1000 \, \Omega$ resistors available, use two of them in series between the battery top lead and earth to feed $V_{-}$: $$V_{-} = V_{batt} \times \frac{1000}{1000+1000} = \frac{V_{batt}}{2}$$ This does not change with temperature. Switching happens when $V_{+} = V_{-}$, i.e. when $R_{th} = 1000 \, \Omega$.

Step 4: **Complete the drawing**
Connect top horizontal wire to the top of both dividers, bottom earthed wire to the bottom of both dividers. Connect the midpoint of the two fixed resistors to the inverting (-) input, and the midpoint of the thermistor (top) and $1000 \, \Omega$ resistor (bottom) to the non-inverting (+) input. No extra connections to the battery or earth.

parts.label: (b)(i)
hints: Hint 1: For $V_{OUT}$ to be -5.0 V you need $V_{+} < V_{-}$. With the circuit in (a), does that need the thermistor resistance to be above or below the $1000 \, \Omega$ balance value at low temperature?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Pick a resistance that keeps $V_{+}$ low**
At low temperature $V_{OUT} = -5.0 \text{ V}$ means $V_{+} < V_{-} = V_{batt}/2$. From $$V_{+} = V_{batt} \times \frac{1000}{R_{th}+1000}$$ this needs $R_{th} > 1000 \, \Omega$. Any sensibly larger NTC value is fine, for example about $1500 \, \Omega$ to $2000 \, \Omega$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: For $V_{OUT}$ to switch to +5.0 V you need $V_{+} > V_{-}$. How must the NTC resistance now compare with $1000 \, \Omega$ after warming?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Pick a resistance that pushes $V_{+}$ high**
At higher temperature $V_{OUT} = +5.0 \text{ V}$ means $V_{+} > V_{-}$. This needs the divider fraction to be greater than one half, so $$R_{th} < 1000 \, \Omega$$ Any sensibly smaller NTC value is fine, for example about $500 \, \Omega$.
